A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DADA, with matching authors, architecture, equations and core experiments. The main text, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original anomaly-detection experiments on nine evaluation datasets, component ablations, parameter sensitivity and pre-training analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains the original experiments and adds UCR evaluation, fine-tuning, synthetic anomaly cases, training without human-labeled anomalies and runtime measurements.

M1.justification: The architecture, complementary masking, adaptive routing, adversarial losses and inference procedure are retained. Although v3 emphasizes synthetic anomalies more strongly, anomaly injection was already used in v1; Appendix A and Table 7 retain the same labeled-data and injected-anomaly sources.

E1.justification: v3 adds the UCR archive's 250 univariate datasets, each containing one anomaly interval, and evaluates anomaly localization on them (Appendices A.1 and C.2). This substantially extends the evaluation scenarios beyond the retained nine datasets. The original pre-training dataset coverage remains unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds MEMTO and SensitiveHUE to the existing 17 baselines. The new UCR comparison evaluates Timer, previously only cited. The revised appendix Table 8 drops DCdetector from the corresponding comparison, although it remains elsewhere. The other established comparator groups are retained.

E3.justification: v3 adds range-based AUC and VUS metrics on three datasets, a quantile-ranking evaluation protocol for UCR, downstream fine-tuning at different training-data fractions, and a control using only injected anomalies. These are substantial additions to the evaluation design; the existing dataset splits and default training settings are retained.

E4.justification: New analyses test fine-tuning under data scarcity, detection of four synthetic anomaly types, dependence on human-labeled anomalies, and inference overhead from multiple bottlenecks (Section 4.3 and Appendices E.1, E.2 and E.4). The earlier component ablations, sensitivity tests, MoE comparison and pre-training-source analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars or statistical tests. The new UCR quantile distribution describes detection performance across datasets, rather than uncertainty across experimental runs.

E6.justification: Shared numerical entries in Tables 1–3 are unchanged, but substantial results are added. UCR results report 166 versus 110 successful datasets for DADA versus Timer at the 3% quantile; new fine-tuning results reach F1 scores of 79.90 on MSL and 85.50 on SMD. Additional baseline, metric, label-free and runtime results appear. The old SMAP/SWaT AUC entries and five-dataset averages disappear, and the bottleneck-selection proportions are revised.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation and Equations (1)–(7) are retained. v3 explicitly restates the gradient-reversal derivative already described in v1, without adding a derivation, formal assumption, theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The central one-model-for-many, zero-shot detection and competitive-performance claims remain. The introduction adds an explicit claim that AdaBN is the first to approach generalization through dynamic bottlenecks, and refines the decoder contribution toward distinguishing normal patterns from common anomalies.

C2.justification: v3 adds the substantive explanation that injected common anomalies prevent overfitting to domain-specific anomalies, alongside interpretations of label-free training, targeted anomaly coverage and acceptable runtime overhead. It also removes Appendix F, including the explicit limitations concerning unmodeled cross-variable correlations and unexplored alternative backbones.

D1.justification: Appendix E.4 newly identifies the bottlenecks as simple MLPs and reports MSL inference times of 4.96 versus 5.29 seconds. Section 4.1 clarifies common baseline metrics and thresholding. Appendix B removes the approximately 1.5-hour training time per epoch, while retaining the other listed hyperparameters and A800 hardware.

R1.justification: v3 adds references for MEMTO, SensitiveHUE, UCR and VUS, and removes Salem et al.'s health-monitoring reference. It also sharpens the dynamic-bottleneck priority claim. The related-work survey and overall positioning remain largely intact; the CAE-Ensemble publication update represents the same work.

P1.justification: Targeted rewrites expand the generalization rationale, gradient-reversal explanation and evaluation description. Appendices C and E gain subsections, while Appendix F is removed. The main section order and much of the existing prose remain unchanged, so this is not a wholesale narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: v3 adds fine-tuning, UCR and anomaly-case figures plus a label-free-results table, substantially redesigns Table 8, and expands Tables 1 and 4. Figure 1 is redrawn; the earlier bottleneck-selection and pre-training-source plots are combined into Figure 11, with an updated bottleneck legend. Title, heading, citation and page-layout styling also change.

improvement.justification: The UCR comparison with Timer, additional evaluation metrics and targeted label-reliance and runtime analyses strengthen evidence for generalization and practical usability. These benefits are moderated by removal of explicit cross-variable and backbone limitations and the SMAP/SWaT AUC results, reducing transparency about remaining weaknesses. Overall, the evidence supports a limited net improvement.
